attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post, not a quotation of anyone else.

semantics.note: 'Cannot possibly' is firm, not hedged. The normalisation keeps the $1 trillion figure and the 'in this environment' condition. Treating it as a conditional forecast tied to the selloff is faithful. The hedged sentence that follows ('may run out of cash') is correctly left out.

contract.note: The plain reading (no completed OpenAI IPO valued at $1 trillion or more while the selloff persists) is ordinary and fair. Using the final offering price as the valuation is reasonable. The condition has no endpoint, but that does not decide the current result because no IPO has happened.

evidence.note: A dated Nov 20 report of an Asian tech selloff. It shows the market condition exists, but it is not evidence about whether OpenAI IPO'd or at what valuation, so it is context only, not support.
Bank research dated Nov 20 on the weak US AI and broad market on Nov 19. It is evidence of the condition only, with nothing on an OpenAI IPO outcome.
OpenAI's own June 2026 disclosure of a confidential S-1 filing. It is a preparatory step with no timing or pricing, so it does not bear on the outcome.

reviews.rationale: This is a firm conditional forecast with no deadline. The evidence shows the selloff condition existed around Nov 19–20, but no OpenAI IPO has been completed or priced by the evaluation date, and none of the items shows one. Not IPO-ing is not a conclusive event under the contract, and the claim was made only two days before evaluation. So it is unresolved.
